Master's degree from an accredited college or university.
Five years of experience in secondary or higher education coordinating day-to-day office, program, or classroom operations, activities, and outcomes.
1.Coordinate development, monitoring, and implementation of annual project work plans, timelines, deliverables, and milestone tracking systems.
2.Lead day-to-day implementation and coordination of initiative activities to ensure completion of annual work plans, deliverables, milestones, and performance objectives.

3.Serve as the primary point of contact for participating districts, colleges, consultants, contractors, evaluators, and project partners regarding implementation activities and ongoing project support.
4.Coordinate statewide technical assistance activities, including coaching sessions, office hours, communities of practice, implementation consultations, and support services.
5.Develop annual statewide professional learning plans and coordinate implementation of convenings, workshops, webinars, trainings, and other learning opportunities.

6.Coordinate agenda development, speaker recruitment, presenter communications, participant registration, event evaluations, and post-event follow-up activities for statewide convenings, professional learning activities, and conferences.
7.Coordinate travel arrangements, lodging, registration, scheduling, meeting logistics, and related operational activities for project staff, consultants, speakers, and participants.
8.Research, prepare, and coordinate conference presentation proposals, speaking opportunities, publications, and dissemination activities aligned with project goals.
9.Develop and maintain project communication systems, including newsletters, implementation updates, calendars, listservs, websites, digital collaboration platforms, and stakeholder communications.

10.Facilitate ongoing communication and engagement among participating districts, colleges, educational partners, state agencies, workforce development organizations, Regional Consortiums, and K-16 Collaboratives.
11.Coordinate and facilitate recurring meetings, office hours, implementation check-ins, stakeholder workgroups, advisory groups, and communities of practice.

12.Lead development, maintenance, implementation, testing, user support, and continuous improvement of project websites, the California Early College Playbook, and other digital resource platforms, collaboration tools, and technology systems supporting the initiative.
13.Coordinate collection, review, organization, and dissemination of implementation tools, templates, case studies, promising practices, publications, and resource materials.
14.Manage project websites, digital resource libraries, implementation repositories, resource-sharing platforms, and related communication tools.
15.Coordinate site visit scheduling, agendas, logistics, facilitation, follow-up activities, and documentation for participating districts and project partners.
16.Support collection and organization of project data, implementation information, participation records, technical assistance activities, and evaluation materials.
17.Prepare draft reports, presentations, implementation summaries, resource guides, communications materials, and project documentation.

18.Monitor implementation progress across participating districts and colleges; identify emerging needs, coordinate technical assistance responses, and facilitate resolution of implementation challenges.
19.Assist with management of consultants, contractors, and project vendors, including monitoring deliverables, coordinating meetings, and supporting project implementation activities.
20.Supervise assigned project staff and coordinate activities among project personnel, consultants, and contractors.
21.Represent the initiative at meetings, conferences, professional development activities, and stakeholder engagement events as assigned.
22.Perform other related activities and duties as assigned.
Project management principles and practices.
Professional learning and technical assistance delivery models.
Event planning, meeting management, and operational logistics.
Budget monitoring, purchasing, contracts, and fiscal procedures.
Communication strategies and stakeholder engagement practices.
Website and digital platform management.
Community college or K-12 systems, educational partnerships, and dual enrollment/early college programs.
Data collection, reporting, and continuous improvement practices.
Coordinate multiple complex projects simultaneously.
Build and maintain collaborative relationships with diverse stakeholders.
Plan and implement professional learning opportunities and large-scale events.
Develop written communications, reports, presentations, and implementation resources.
Organize and maintain detailed project records and documentation.
Facilitate meetings and collaborative workgroups.
Manage competing priorities and timelines effectively.
Work independently while supporting a large multi-partner initiative.
Supervise and coordinate the work of assigned staff.
Demonstrated sensitivity to and understanding of the diverse academic, socioeconomic, cultural, ethnic, and disability backgrounds of community college students and employees.
Communicate effectively both orally and in writing.
